marta: Heads-up: after the checkpoint bump to model-checkpoint-v4.1, p99 gen latency jumped ~2.3x on staging. CI perf job flagged it and we auto-paused the rollout.
liam: ugh — is this tokenization-related or a serving change?
sree: I pulled a quick perf profile from the staging box. Allocation looks normal, but kernel selection metrics show a lot more fallbacks to the slow attention kernel for batches > 512 tokens.
marta: here's the short profiling snippet (staging run @ 1951232000):
```
profile: gen_p99 312ms -> 720ms
kernel_selector: fused_attn_hits=342, fused_attn_fallbacks=1289
kv_cache: prefix_hit_rate=0.91 -> 0.67
batch_sizes: 16/32/64 distribution shifted right after tokenizer map change
```
kai: interesting — tokenizer mapping change could change token lengths and fragment sequences, which would both bump batching and blow the KV hit rate. Any PRs touching tokenizer or selector recently?
marta: bisect points at two merges around the same time: PR #1287 (batching heuristics + selector thresholds) and PR #1299 (tokenizer map update for new checkpoint). CI shows perf regression only when both are present.
liam: that smells like an interaction: tokenizer changes increase average sequence length -> different batch packing -> kernel selector picks fallback for longer sequences -> more KV evictions and lower prefix hit rate -> p99 spike.
sree: I repro'd locally by swapping in the new tokenizer but keeping old selector thresholds — p99 stays low. Swapping the selector thresholds back to pre-PR state while keeping new tokenizer reduces p99 by ~30%.
kai: can we hotfix by reverting the selector threshold change and re-running the rollout? Or pin the tokenizer map for the checkpoint? Which is lower risk?
marta: selector revert is smaller surface area and should be quick. I'll open a revert PR for #1287 and roll a canary with the new checkpoint + old selector.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for model-checkpoint-v4.1 (run id: r-2026-03-18-001). Manual action required to resume.
liam: add a CI perf test that runs the staging prompt set with both tokenizer variants and asserts kernel selection ratio doesn't regress more than 10% — that should catch this in future.
sree: also adding a monitoring alert for kv_cache.prefix_hit_rate drop > 5% during shadow rollouts.
kai: quick experiment: switched the canary to quantized-compat (smaller KV footprint) and p99 dropped back to ~1.1x baseline. Not ideal but helps as a mitigation.
marta: plan: 1) open revert PR for #1287 (doing now), 2) re-run canary with new checkpoint + reverted selector, 3) add CI perf test and alert, 4) re-evaluate a safer selector rollout after we understand tokenizer distribution. I'll post updates here. @eng-oncall please triage if any production hits. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks — if revert looks good, we can unpause the rollout. Also file a follow-up to redesign selector to be robust to tokenizer distribution shifts (maybe use a rolling stat on seq len).
marta: noted. opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1315 (revert of 1287).
